'''Burkhard Heim''' ({{IPA|de|haɪm|lang}}; 9 February 1925 – 14 January 2001) was a German theoretical [[physicist]] known for proposing a [[unified field theory]] called [[Heim theory]], which he claimed could have applications to the development of [[Hyperspace|hyperspace travel]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Lietz |first=Haiko |date=4 January 2006 |title=Take a leap into hyperspace |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg18925331-200-take-a-leap-into-hyperspace/ |access-date=2024-04-16 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Ludwiger">{{cite web|last = von Ludwiger|first = Illobrand|date = 28 January 2001|title = Zum Tode des Physikers Burkhard Heim|location=Feldkirchen-Westerham|url=http://www.mufon-ces.org/text/deutsch/heim.htm|language=de}}</ref>

==Academic and work history==
===1940s===
In 1943, Heim met [[Werner Heisenberg]], a [[Germany|German]] physicist involved in [[atom bomb]] research, and told him of his plan to use a form of chemical [[Implosion (mechanical process)|implosion]] to facilitate an atomic explosion. This [[design]] was based on an idea he developed for a 'clean' [[hydrogen bomb]] when he was 18. Heisenberg was impressed by Heim's knowledge, but thought the approach would be impractical.<ref name="Ludwiger"/>

At the start of [[World War II]], Heim avoided conscription into the [[German Air Force]] by working in a chemical laboratory as an explosives technician. When he was 19, an explosion in the laboratory caused by the mishandling of unstable compounds left him without hands and mostly [[Hearing impairment|deaf]] and [[blindness|blind]].<ref name=":0" /> Heim underwent the [[Krukenberg procedure|Krukenberg Procedure]] after the accident.{{fact|date=June 2025}}

After World War II, Heim registered to study physics at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=":0" />

===1950s===
In 1952, during the third congressional session of the [[International Astronautical Federation]] (IAF) in Stuttgart, Germany, Heim presented his theory for interplanetary propulsion under the title of "''Die dynamische Kontrabarie als Lösung des astronomischen Problems''" (The Dynamic Kontrabarie as Solution of the Astronautical Problem).<ref name="Weyla">{{cite journal|last = Weyl|first = A. R.|date = October 1957|title = Anti-gravity|journal = Aeronautics|volume = 37|number = 2|pages = 80–86|publisher = British Aviation Publications}}</ref>  It was the first time the idea of gravitational, electromagnetic, weak, and strong forces were treated as distortions of their proper [[Euclidean distance|Euclidean metrics]] in a higher-dimensional space.<ref>{{cite conference |url = http://www.hpcc-space.com/publications/documents/PrinciplesOfAdvancedSpacePropulsionAIAA-paper-2002-4094.pdf|title= Physical principles of advanced space propulsion based on Heim's field theory|first1= W.|last1= Dröscher|first2 = J.|last2 = Häuser|date= July 2002|conference= 38th AIAA/ASME/SAE/ASEE Joint Propulsion Conference & Exhibit|conference-url= http://arc.aiaa.org/doi/book/10.2514/MJPC02|id=2002-4094|publisher= [[AIAA]]|location= Indianapolis, Indiana|access-date= 7 July 2015}}</ref>  A brief description of Heim's lecture was recorded in the proceedings of the Society for Space Research.<ref name="Weylb">{{cite book|last = Weyl|first = A. R.|date = January 1959|chapter = Knowledge and possibilities of gravity research|translator = W. R. Eichler|title = Weltraumfahrt; Zeitschrift für Rakententechnik|language = de|orig-year = 1958|pages = 100–106|volume = 9|id = DTIC No. AD-0830247}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last = Weyl|first = A. R|date = February 1959|title = Gravity and the prospects for astronautics|journal = Aeronautics|volume = 59|issue = 6|pages = 16–22|publisher = British Aviation Publications}}</ref>

In 1954, he began to study under [[Carl Friedrich von Weizsäcker]] in [[Göttingen]].<ref name="Ludwiger"/>  He wrote his diploma thesis on physical processes in the [[Crab Nebula]] [[Supernova]]. Then, he began to work at the [[Max Planck Institute]] for [[Astrophysics]] in Göttingen. However, he soon found it extremely difficult to work in a team due to his disabilities.{{cn|date=May 2023}}

In 1955, Heim was contracted by the [[Glenn L. Martin Company]] to assist them with a gravity control propulsion project.<ref name="Talbert">{{cite news|last = Talbert|first = A. E.|date = 30 November 1955|title = Conquest of gravity aim of top scientists in U.S.|newspaper = New York Herald-Tribune|pages = 1, 36}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last = Talbert|first = A. E.|date = 30 November 1955|title = Scientists taking first steps in assault on gravity barrier|newspaper = The Miami Herald|pages = 1, 2–A}}</ref>  The news about Heim's contract was published during a period of increasing [[United States gravity control propulsion research (1955 - 1974)]].<ref name="Talbert" />

In 1956, Heim completed a 27-page progress report that summarized his philosophy (syntrometry) and his theory (Principle of Dynamic Kontrabarie) for coupling general relativity with [[quantum dynamics]] for propulsion applications.<ref>{{cite thesis|last = Watson|first = J. T.|date = February 1961|title = Gravitational control research|type = Master's|id = DTIC No. AD-0253588}}</ref>  Sample calculations for an expedition from the surface of the Earth to the surface of the planet [[Mars]] appeared at the end of Heim's progress report.

In November 1957, Heim delivered a lecture about his propulsion theory to the [[Verein für Raumschiffahrt|German Society for Rocket Technology and Space Travel]] in Frankfurt.<ref name="Ludwiger" />  Subsequently, [[Wernher von Braun]] sought his comments on various aerospace projects.<ref name="Lietz">{{cite news |last=Lietz |first=Haiko |date=5 January 2006 |title=Take a leap into hyperspace |volume=189 |newspaper=New Scientist |issue=2533 |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg18925331.200-take-a-leap-into-hyperspace.html |url-access=subscription}}</ref>  According to von Ludwiger, a German author known for his publication on [[Unidentified flying object|UFOs]], an audiotape of Heim's presentation had been prepared for shipment to America.<ref name="Ludwiger" />

In 1959, Heim completed his first publication in the German journal ''Zeitschrift für Flugkörper'' (''Magazine for Missiles'').<ref name="Robertson">{{cite journal|last1 = Robertson|first1 = G. A.|last2 = Murad|first2 = P. A.|last3 = Davis|first3 = E.|date = 2008|title = New frontiers in space propulsion sciences|journal = Energy Conversion and Management|volume = 49|issue = 3|pages = 436–452|doi=10.1016/j.enconman.2007.10.013| bibcode=2008ECM....49..436R }}</ref><ref name="Heima">{{cite journal|last = Heim|first = B.|date = 1959|title = Das Prinzip der dynamischen Kontrabarie|journal = Zeitschrift für Flugkörper|language = de|volume = 1|number = 4|pages = 100–02}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last = Heim|first = B.|date = 1959|title = Das Prinzip der dynamischen Kontrabarie (II)|journal = Zeitschrift für Flugkörper|language = de|volume = 1|number = 6|pages = 164–66}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last = Heim|first = B.|date = 1959|title = Das Prinzip der dynamischen Kontrabarie (III)|journal = Zeitschrift für Flugkörper|language = de|volume = 1|number = 7|pages = 219–21}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last = Heim|first = B.|date = 1959|title = Das Prinzip der dynamischen Kontrabarie (IV)|journal = Zeitschrift für Flugkörper|language = de|volume = 1|number = 8|pages = 244–48}}</ref>  Heim discussed "the principle of the dynamic "Kontrabarie," examining how a field drive would be more effective than the best chemical drive for rockets." These papers remained ambiguous on the fundamental concepts underlying his theory of the field drive, likely the calculations on the extra fields of his field theory remained unsolved. These calculations were only performed a few years later.<ref name="Heima" />

Heim stopped working on the propulsion aspect of his theory in 1959. He spent the remainder of his life devoted to refining the unified field attributes of his theory.<ref name="Lietz" />

===1960s===
In the late 1950s and early 1960s, there were a number of reports on Heim in magazines and [[tabloid (newspaper format)|tabloids]] such as ''Le Figaro'', ''Bunte Illustrierte'', ''Quick'' and ''[[Stern (magazine)|Stern]]''. The magazine ''[[le Figaro]]'' remarked, on 15 January 1969, that he was an "inhuman robot".<ref name="Ludwiger"/>  The German television station [[ARD (broadcaster)|ARD]] ran reports and interviews with Heim. It was speculated that Heim was likely to make a breakthrough, either in fundamental physics or propulsion theory.

On 17 November 1969, Heim reported the progress he had made towards developing his unified field theory to [[Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm]] (MBB). [[Pascual Jordan]] and Gebhard Lyra were among the small body of scientists who attended that colloquium. Jordan wrote Heim a letter on 22 December 1969, encouraging him to publish his theory.<ref name="Ludwiger"/>

===1970s===
[[Ludwig Bölkow]] encouraged Heim to enhance his theory.<ref name="Lietz"/>  On 25 November 1976, Heim publicly introduced, for the first time, his completed unified field theory in a presentation to MBB engineers.<ref>{{cite speech|last = Heim|first = Burkhard|translator = Jim Graham|translator2 = John Reed|date = 2008|orig-year = 1976|title = Basic Thoughts on a unified field theory of matter and gravity (Version 1.2)|url = https://www.engon.de/protosimplex/downloads/02%20heim%20-%20mbb%201.2en.pdf|event = MBB presentation|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>  It included the methodology for calculating the mass spectrum of [[Elementary particle|elementary particles]]. Pursuant to recommendations by [[Werner Heisenberg]]'s successor, [[Hans-Peter Dürr]], Heim published his unified field theory summary the following year in an article entitled "Recommendations of a Way to a Unified Description of Elementary Particles" in the Max Planck Institute journal ''Zeitschrift für Naturforschung'' (Journal of Natural Research).<ref>{{cite journal|last = Heim|first = B.|date = 1977|title = Vorschlag eines Weges einer einheitlichen Beschreibung der Elementarteilchen|language = de|journal = Zeitschrift für Naturforschung|volume = 23a|pages = 233–243| doi=10.1515/zna-1977-3-404 | s2cid=100902276 |doi-access = free}}</ref>  This was the first publication of his theory in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

===1980s===
In 1982, Heim's mass formula was programmed on a computer at the German Electron Synchrotron [[DESY]] in Hamburg with the assistance of some resident scientists.<ref name="Lietz"/>  Up to that point, Heim had not yet confided in other [[theoretical physicist]]s on the details of the mass formula derivation. Hence, the DESY results were not widely published and disseminated for academic scrutiny. That year Walter Dröscher, a theorist at the Vienna Patent Office, began to work with Heim. The first result of their collaboration culminated in the second volume of Heim's major work, appearing in 1984.<ref name="Lietz"/>

===2000s===
Heim died in [[Northeim]] in 2001 at age 75.

In 2004, the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA) awarded the winning paper in the nuclear and future flight field to a retired Austrian patent officer named Walter Dröscher and Jochem Häuser, a physicist and professor of computer science at the University of Applied Sciences in Salzgitter, Germany. They turned the theoretical framework of Burkhard Heim into a proposal for an experimental test for a propulsion device that is thought to theoretically be able to travel at rates [[faster-than-light|faster than the speed of light]]. Hans Theodor Auerbach, a theoretical physicist and colleague of Heim has stated that, "As far as I understand it, Heim theory is ingenious," and, "I think that physics will take this direction in the future".<ref name="Lietz"/><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.hpcc-space.de/publications/documents/aiaa2004-3700-a4.pdf|title = Guidelines For A Space Propulsion Device Based On Heim's Quantum Theory|website = HPCC-Space GmbH}}</ref>

In 2008, the AIAA Nuclear and Future Flight Propulsion Technical Committee published the following statement:

::Much research was conducted this year on the investigation of the experimental basis of the existence of gravity-like fields that cannot be described by conventional gravitation; that is, by the accumulation of mass. Investigations emphasized a geometrized approach termed Extended Heim Theory, which extends Einstein's idea of geometrization of physics by employing the additional concepts of Heim.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Donahue, B. |author2=Moton-Nkhata, T. |author3=the AIAA Nuclear |author4=Future Flight Propulsion Committee |name-list-style=amp |date = December 2008|title = Nuclear and future flight propulsion|journal = Aerospace America|pages = 57–59|url = http://www.hpcc-space.de/publications/documents/AerospaceAmericaAdvancedPropulsionDec2008.pdf}}</ref>

==Life and health==
Heim had to undergo a series of at least 50 operations after a laboratory explosion that resulted in the loss of both of his hands.<ref name="QUANTHOMME 2009">{{cite web | title=CHERCHEURS, THEORICIENS H-P | website=QUANT'HOMME | date=12 March 2009 | url=http://quanthomme.free.fr/energielibre/chercheurs/CHERCHEURS2.htm | language=fr | access-date=21 March 2022 |quote=Victim of a laboratory accident during the Second World War, Burkhard Heim had both hands amputated. He was also suffering from advanced deafness and almost total blindness. It took more than 50 operations to restore some of his abilities.}}</ref> He had found that intense concentration on the study of Einstein's relativity theory had helped him control the pain in his arms mentally and physically.

The loss of his hands and serious reduction of his eyesight apparently resulted in Heim acquiring an [[Eidetic memory|eidetic]], acoustic memory.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} He was said to rarely forget a formula if he heard it recited, and he was said to be able to learn a language in a matter of days. He married a former concert singer from [[Prague]] in 1950 named Gerda.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

== Heim theory ==
'''Heim theory''' was proposed by Heim in 1957 as an attempt to develop a [[theory of everything]] in [[theoretical physics]]. The theory claims to bridge some of the disagreements between [[quantum mechanics]] and [[general relativity]].<ref name="long">{{cite book |last=Long |first=Kelvin F. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EAD2-GrarkEC&q=Heim+theory&pg=PA295 |title=Deep Space Propulsion: A Roadmap to Interstellar Flight |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]] |year=2012 |isbn=978-1461406075 |pages=295–296 |format=Google Books preview}}</ref> The theory has received little attention in the scientific literature and is regarded as being outside mainstream science<ref name="newsci">{{cite news |last=Lietz |first=Haiko |date=5 January 2006 |title=Take a leap into hyperspace |url=https://www.bibliotecapleyades.net/ciencia/ciencia_hyperdimensions11.htm |access-date=2013-07-20 |newspaper=[[New Scientist]] magazine |publisher=Reed Business Information Ltd. |format=Full text article available for free download. |quote=...the idea relies on an obscure and largely unrecognized kind of physics...The majority of physicists have never heard of Heim theory, and most of those contacted by New Scientist said they couldn't make sense of Dröscher and Häuser's description of the theory behind their proposed experiment...The general consensus seems to be that Dröscher and Häuser's theory is incomplete at best...it has not passed any normal form of peer review.}}</ref><ref name="long" /><ref name="drow">{{cite web |author1=Citation rates |author2=other information |date=20 July 2013 |title=Dröscher, W. |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Dr%C3%B6scher%2C+W.&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C22&as_sdtp= |access-date=2013-07-20 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref><ref name="giov">{{cite book |last1=Modanese | first1=Giovanni | last2=Robertson | first2=Glen A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YafxlC5hL0UC&q=%22heim+theory%22+physics&pg=PA231 |title=Gravity-Superconductors Interactions: Theory and Experiment |publisher=[[Bentham Science Publishers]] |year=2012 |isbn=978-1608054008 |pages=230–231 |format=Google Books preview}}</ref> but has attracted some interest in popular and fringe media.<ref name="giov" /><ref>{{cite book |last=Farrell |first=Joseph P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UvSGUxT76NkC&q=%22heim+theory%22+physics&pg=PA111 |title=Babylon's Banksters: The Alchemy of Deep Physics, High Finance and Ancient Religion |publisher=[[Feral House]] |year=2010 |isbn=978-1932595796 |location=Port Townsend, WA |pages=110–111}}</ref><ref name="ufo">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=E2hO2WIlgS0C&q=%22heim+theory%22+physics&pg=PA42 |title=Ufos For Know-It-Alls |publisher=Filiquarian Publishing |year=2008 |isbn=978-1599862323 |pages=41}}{{Dead link|date=October 2023|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> Heim attempted to resolve incompatibilities between [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] and [[general relativity]]. To meet that goal, he developed a mathematical approach based on quantizing [[spacetime]].<ref name="newsci" />

Heim's theory also predicts the existence of two hypothetical [[neutrino]]s, which have been shown not to exist by experiments at the [[Large Electron–Positron Collider]].<ref>{{cite web|first = Olaf|last = Posdzech|url = http://www.worlditc.org/f_06_protosimplex_heim_a_biography.htm|title = Burkhard Heim, a biography}}</ref><ref name="L31992">{{cite journal | title = Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species | journal=Physics Letters B | year = 1992|author=over four hundred co-authors | collaboration = L3 Collaboration | volume = 292 | issue = 3–4 | pages = 463–471|bibcode = 1992PhLB..292..463A |doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(92)91204-M | hdl=2066/26827 | url=https://sedici.unlp.edu.ar/handle/10915/73124 | hdl-access = free }}</ref>
